steps.content: "When others weigh the pros and cons, and exhaust themselves with schemes... When you see the depravity and cruelty of this world..." "Anniken, how will you maintain your righteousness and sincerity?"
Miss Rise Blake, welcome to the interview! I hope you got here smoothly?
Clad in virtual equipment, Rise stands in the center of the VR squash court, waiting for the serve prompt with a simulated racket in hand.
She stares straight ahead as faces from her memories flicker on the wall across from her.

steps.speaker: Interviewer A
steps.content: We saw your resume on DisHire. Elite Eastside graduate, top of your class...

steps.speaker: Interviewer B
steps.content: Both your personal qualities and experience at Nirvana align perfectly with the position we're hiring for. That's why we contacted you immediately!

steps.speaker: Interviewer C
steps.content: Our company just got listed at the beginning of the year. Though we're not large, we work with many established corporations in Eastside, and we're growing rapidly. We really welcome young talent like you to join us.
Different genders and faces, all bearing the same mass-produced smile. The effect is absurd and surreal.
"They" simultaneously open their mouths.

steps.speaker: Interviewers
steps.content: But...

steps.speaker: Interviewer A
steps.content: You only have an undergraduate degree, which is a bit below our expectations. But I believe you have great potential.

steps.speaker: Interviewer A
steps.content: Our company places great value on talent development. It's best for undergraduates to get some entry-level experience first. This gives you more room for advancement later.
The serve prompt sounds. Rise swiftly swings the racket and hits the squash ball with extraordinary force.

steps.speaker: Rise
steps.content: I completely agree. Entry-level experience is certainly important.

steps.speaker: Rise
steps.content: Without it, you'd have no excuse to cut the salary offer and change job descriptions on the spot. Or maybe just put "pig in a poke" in your ad next time? Doesn't sound as nice, but certainly more fitting.
A face on the wall gets hit by the squash ball, shattering it to pieces.

steps.speaker: Interviewer B
steps.content: Our regulations require an on-site test for this role. It's to assess your abilities before your probation begins.

steps.speaker: Interviewer B
steps.content: Um... the test is quite challenging, but it's to evaluate your stress resistance. Don't worry too much about it.

steps.speaker: Rise
steps.content: So, you mean after passing the test, there's still a one-year probation period? Isn't your talent acquisition process a tad too inefficient?

steps.speaker: Rise
steps.content: How do you survive in Eastside without going bankrupt? Oh... by using these test scams? That's indeed a good way to reduce costs and increase output.

steps.speaker: Interviewer C
steps.content: Young people ought to have the passion of youth. It's true that Saturdays aren't mentioned in the contract, but you've got to look beyond the surface.

steps.speaker: Interviewer C
steps.content: Delve deeper... if you work just one more day a week than others in Eastside, this adds up to fifty days a year. Bit by bit, this takes you ahead of the curve! You'll benefit greatly...

steps.speaker: Rise
steps.content: Absolutely right. Your words truly enlighten me.

steps.speaker: Rise
steps.content: The leaders of the company must set a great example for everyone, right? Twelve hours a day with no holidays, at the very least...

steps.speaker: Rise
steps.content: You think I'm kicking up a fuss? No, delve deeper. I'm actually offering you an ingenious proposal on how to stay ahead of the curve in DisCity.
With a leap and swing, yet another face disappears from the wall. Unfazed by fatigue, each of Rise's hits is stronger than the last.
The pressure from all the interviews desperately needs an outlet, driving Rise to raise her arm once more.

steps.speaker: Interviewer D
steps.content: Can you elaborate on the projects you worked on at Nirvana?

steps.speaker: Rise
steps.content: I've detailed all my project experience in my resume. May I ask which specific project you're interested in?

steps.speaker: Interviewer D
steps.content: ...No, no, those are already quite clear. We know you've worked at Nirvana for quite some time, so you must have some more "in-depth" and "long-term" insights about Nirvana, right?

steps.speaker: Rise
steps.content: They're all such hideous fools.
Suddenly, a piercing alarm jolts her back to reality. Rise realizes that the VR device has abruptly stopped her squash session because she was pushing herself too hard.
The light and particles that burst from her body during the emotional outburst vanish instantly. In the late-night VR squash court, she finds herself alone, as if the incident never occurred.
Anniken replies: "I will use my lightsaber to cut through the filth and tear apart evil. The blade will guide me out of injustice and darkness." "I firmly believe in this."

steps.speaker: New Boss
steps.content: Rise, how is the recent work you've taken on? Got any problems?

steps.speaker: Rise
steps.content: None. I'll submit the phased results for next quarter's digital model development before I leave today.

steps.speaker: New Boss
steps.content: You're incredibly efficient. Delegating tasks to you gives me peace of mind. I've gone over the plan you handed in last week—it was very well done. Only a few details need to be fine-tuned.

steps.speaker: New Boss
steps.content: Once you've settled in more and pass your probation, I'll put you in charge of core business... Don't push yourself too hard, and feel free to ask questions anytime, okay?
After countless interviews with all sorts of characters, Rise has finally joined a new company.
The commute is convenient, and the contract is legit. Though the salary isn't high, the workplace is congenial. Her immediate supervisor recognizes her abilities and values her highly.

steps.speaker: Rise
steps.content: For now, working here is the best choice. There's only a few days left before my probation ends. I should be able to pass easily.

steps.speaker: Rise
steps.content: Now... it's time to leave work.
After submitting the results, Rise gathers her things and gets ready to leave. However, a sound from the workstation across from her catches her attention.

steps.speaker: Intern
steps.content: I-I'm really sorry! There's still a bit left, and I might not be able to finish it today. Can I submit this report to you tomorrow? I will definitely finish it tomorrow!

steps.speaker: New Boss
steps.content: Have you considered how much your late submission will delay other colleagues? If you knew you weren't going to finish, why didn't you give me a heads-up?

steps.speaker: Intern
steps.content: I'm sorry, I miscalculated the time... I only received this task this morning, and only later did I realize that it's too much to finish in one day...

steps.speaker: New Boss
steps.content: I care about the results, not the process. You've been interning here for some time now, yet I haven't seen any progress from you.

steps.speaker: New Boss
steps.content: I still remember how well you performed during your interview! The department has always valued you, giving you all sorts of tasks to help you grow in the long run...

steps.speaker: New Boss
steps.content: But look at you now! You're so far from meeting our expectations!
The manager doesn't lower his voice at all. His scolding draws attention from all over the office.
The manager, who is usually gentle and kind to Rise, is now relentlessly scolding the frightened intern. The intern's face turns ashen from shame, but still musters the courage to speak up.

steps.speaker: Intern
steps.content: It's my first time dealing with this type of work, and no one trained me how to do it. I had to figure it out myself, which took a lot of time...

steps.speaker: New Boss
steps.content: Enough with the excuses! No one is guiding the other newbies either, yet they manage to complete their work beautifully. Why is it that you can't do the same?

steps.speaker: Intern
steps.content: I can do it... Can I just have some more time, please? I promise I'll do it well...!

steps.speaker: New Boss
steps.content: You know you're being compared to others, right? If they hit the ground running while you struggle for more time, that calls your competence into question. What's worse, you make excuses instead of facing up to your problems, which means you have an attitude problem as well!

steps.speaker: New Boss
steps.content: The worst thing you can have is an attitude problem! Sigh... I really thought better of you.

steps.speaker: New Boss
steps.content: I'm scolding you now because I'd like to give you a chance... If you still can't own up to your mistakes, then you're truly hopeless!
The young intern is frozen on the spot with nervously clenched shoulders. Her eyes flicker upwards, but she doesn't dare blink.
But the moment she opens her mouth, tears stream uncontrollably down her cheeks.

steps.speaker: Intern
steps.content: I'm sorry, I've caused you trouble. I'm wrong, I'm really sorry...
Rise observes all of this coldly, feeling a familiar, nauseating sense of discord.
Besides, you're in no position to be uppity.
You think a big company like Nirvana can't squash a little intern like you?
The past and the present are the same. It's just that before, she was the victim, and now she's an observer.
She thought she found respect and equality here, but it was all just a hidden bribe, luring her to become a beneficiary, luring her to become part of the facade...
...and luring her to become an accomplice to workplace bullying.

steps.speaker: Rise
steps.content: It's the same everywhere. How disgusting...

steps.speaker: New Boss
steps.content: Alright, enough with your apologizing... Well, I'll give you another chance to make up for it.
The manager lets the intern "earnestly reflect" for a while before letting her go. He then notices Rise's gaze, thinks of something, and points at her.

steps.speaker: New Boss
steps.content: Look at Rise! She's the most capable newcomer I've hired in years, and she's not much older than you. Have you seen how thorough and detailed her proposals are? Why can't you even do half of what she does?

steps.speaker: New Boss
steps.content: Sigh, didn't you complain that no one trained you? Her workstation is right across from you. Why didn't you take the initiative to ask? Why wait for me?
He glares at the intern in frustration, then immediately changes his tone, to address Rise warmly.

steps.speaker: New Boss
steps.content: Rise, this intern's report is really not up to par! You're the best at this in the whole department. Why don't you stay a bit and teach her? With you guiding her, she's bound to improve.
Beaming confidently, the manager sends the report to Rise, as if certain she won't refuse. The intern watches cautiously from the side.
Rise doesn't respond immediately. She opens the document, skims through, then replies.

steps.speaker: Rise
steps.content: I refuse.

steps.speaker: New Boss
steps.content: Alright then, when you finish revising the report tonight... What did you just say?

steps.speaker: Rise
steps.content: I said, no. This isn't within the scope of my work. I don't accept such unreasonable overtime.

steps.speaker: New Boss
steps.content: What overtime... it won't take long! Someone as capable as you can just show the intern how it's done in no time.

steps.speaker: Rise
steps.content: I can do my job well because I respect it and am willing to put in my best effort to complete what's within my responsibilities.

steps.speaker: Rise
steps.content: But I have no obligation or desire to take on irrelevant tasks outside of work.
As Rise refuses the manager's request, she hands a packet of tissues to the stunned intern.

steps.speaker: Rise
steps.content: You don't need to work overtime either. That report isn't as urgent as he says. The department won't stop functioning without an intern's assignment.

steps.speaker: Intern
steps.content: Huh? But, but I still feel like I should...

steps.speaker: New Boss
steps.content: Rise, I know you're young and feisty, but the department is a team. Even if her tasks are lighter, she's still a team member. There shouldn't be a line between what's considered part of one's responsibilities and what's not.
Having lost face, the department manager looks displeased, but still forces a smile.

steps.speaker: New Boss
steps.content: If you don't help her with this report, she won't get it done today. In the bigger picture, it will affect the entire department's schedule.

steps.speaker: Rise
steps.content: Then what are the standards for completing it well or not?

steps.speaker: Rise
steps.content: I've been working longer than her and have more experience. Using me as a standard for this intern is already expecting more than what she is capable of.

steps.speaker: New Boss
steps.content: Cough cough, it's just a goal I hope she works toward. I believe she can do better. That's why I set high standards for her.

steps.speaker: Rise
steps.content: ...I really don't want to hear any more lofty justifications.
She steps forward, places her hands on the table, and looks directly at him, not bothering to hide her annoyance.

steps.speaker: Rise
steps.content: Goals? High standards? I've looked over the intern's assignment already, and it's not urgent enough to require completion today. In fact, she should have ample time for revisions.

steps.speaker: Rise
steps.content: Her current version does have shortcomings, but as a new intern, she's already done her best.

steps.speaker: Rise
steps.content: She has fulfilled her responsibilities and deserves respect, and should not be unfairly targeted by someone using their position as leverage like you.
Rise's words are cold and blunt, surprising everyone with their boldness. Even the manager breaks into a sweat.

steps.speaker: New Boss
steps.content: You... Is this the attitude you should have towards your superior? Rise Blake, before you demand respect, have you respected me?

steps.speaker: Rise
steps.content: It has nothing to do with hierarchy. I believe respect should be equal and mutual.

steps.speaker: Rise
steps.content: But there's one thing you're right about. It's really hard for me to see someone like you as my superior. I'm going to HR to resign now.
With a faint sneer, she turns and leaves the office without looking back.
Seconds later, footsteps echo behind her as the manager catches up. Suppressing his voice and temper, he tries to negotiate nicely.

steps.speaker: New Boss
steps.content: You young folks and your fiery tempers! Think about it, Rise, have I ever mistreated you during your time here? Has the company mistreated you?

steps.speaker: New Boss
steps.content: The department has always valued talented employees like you. Plus, your probation is almost over...

steps.speaker: Rise
steps.content: I don't need preferential treatment at the expense of others. I can't work at a place where employees don't receive equal respect.

steps.speaker: New Boss
steps.content: Is it really necessary to make a fuss over an intern who has nothing to do with you?

steps.speaker: Rise
steps.content: Yet who didn't start out as an intern?
"Brave Anniken, please answer me one more question." "Beyond the injustice and darkness, is it the justice and light you seek, or..." "Another endless abyss?"
Leaving work on time, but no longer employed... This seems to have happened another time just recently.
Rise steps out of the office building and into the crowd leaving work. In an instant, she is gripped by indescribable fatigue and confusion.

steps.speaker: Middle-Aged Colleague
steps.content: Resign? Now? I really don't understand you young people.

steps.speaker: Middle-Aged Colleague
steps.content: Girls like you are too stubborn. After hitting a few walls, you'll realize it's the same everywhere. This company is already quite good by comparison!

steps.speaker: Rise
steps.content: Is it really impossible to find a suitable job anywhere? Am I really the problem?
The words of the colleague who helped with her resignation echo in Rise's mind. She stops at the intersection amidst the surging crowd.

steps.speaker: Rise
steps.content: I just want a fair and positive environment to work in.

steps.speaker: Rise
steps.content: Ha, but most companies in Eastside can't even obey DisCity's most basic labor regulations.

steps.speaker: Rise
steps.content: ...Anniken, are my standards really too high?
"I don't know." "I don't know what lies beyond the injustice and darkness."
Rise?
Suddenly, someone pats Rise on the shoulder from behind, interrupting her chaotic thoughts.
Rise turns around and sees a familiar gray figure.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: It really is you! What a coincidence.

steps.speaker: Rise
steps.content: Oh, it's you, Chief.

steps.speaker: Rise
steps.content: Long time no see. What brings you here at this hour?

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: I happened to be on a mission nearby, and took a stroll after finishing it... How about you? How have you been lately? Is the job search going well?
Rise is silent for a moment, then shakes her head in exasperation. The box full of office supplies in her hands answers the question.
The MBCC Chief thinks for a moment, then extends a hand to Rise.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: Hmm... if you don't mind, I have a suggestion.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: Rise, are you interested in working for the MBCC?
Anniken raises the lightsaber in his hands. "But the lightsaber will guide me to find companions. I shall not walk alone down this path." "I am not the lonely one."
